To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the accumulation of atrial natal peptide and its release in the secretory cardiomyocytes in the right atrium of the rats with renovascular hypertension and sodium loading are different.

the accumulation and excretion from myocyte granule stores of atrial natalyse peptide (ANP) in cardiomyocytes of the rat right atrium are regulated by different mechanisms in experimental renovascular hypertension and in rats with high salt loading.
in experimental hypertension, the secretion of atrial peptides is regulated by different mechanisms depending on the pathogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and excretion of ANP in the secretory cardiomyocytes of the right ventricle in rat models of experimental hypertension.
the synthesis and excretion of ANP by cardiomyocytes of the right and left atria in rats with experimental hypertension.
the synthesis and excretion of the atrial natriurotic peptide in secretory cardiomyocytes in experimental hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the case of hypertension the atrial natriuresis is not a major factor in the control of arterial blood pressure.
the atrial natriuritic peptide plays an important role in the regulation of water and electrolyte metabolism and in maintaining normal arterial pressure.

atrial natri uretic peptide secretion in cardiomyocytes is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon, and that the regulatory mechanisms of the process can be different and depend on the etiology of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the secretion of ANP in cardiomyocytes is not directly associated with high BP, but rather with the development of hypertension.
in the case of renovascular hypertension the accumulation of atrial nataliuretic peptide in cardiomyocytes is not accompanied by an increased release of peptide into the circulation.

the accumulation of atrial natiuretic peptide in secretory cardiomyocytes of the right ventricle is a compensatory mechanism of the organism in response to increased blood pressure and is not a specific marker of the development of renovascular hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in renovascular hypertension, atrial natriurotic peptide is synthesized and secreted in secretory cardiomyocytes, whereas in salt-dependent hypertension, the peptide is synthesized in atrial myocytes and released into the blood.
in the case of salt-dependent hypertension, the secretion of atrial peptide is regulated by the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.
in experimental hypertension, the synthesis of atrial natiuretic peptide by myocytes of the heart right atrium occurs and that it is accompanied by the release of the peptide into the blood.
